description: Task-13 grounding corpus — architect-AUTHORED paraphrased summaries of ISO 45001:2018 clause requirements. NO verbatim ISO text (owner licensing decision 2026-07-05: tenants upload their own licensed copies; eval grounding uses corpus-consistent paraphrase). Wording is independent of the eval set's paraphrasedRequirement fields to avoid string-overlap circularity.

docs.text: The organization has to work out which internal and external issues matter to its purpose and could help or hinder the intended results of its occupational health and safety management system — things like workforce profile, contractual arrangements, regulatory climate, and site conditions.

Beyond workers, the organization must identify the other interested parties relevant to the OH&S system — regulators, unions, contractors, visitors, neighbours — and determine which of their needs and expectations become compliance obligations it chooses or is required to meet.

The organization defines the boundaries and applicability of its OH&S management system to set its scope, taking into account the context issues, the obligations owed to interested parties, and the planned work-related activities; the scope must cover activities that can impact OH&S performance and be available as documented information.
An OH&S management system, with the processes it needs and their interactions, must be established, implemented, maintained and continually improved in line with the standard's requirements.

Top management must demonstrate leadership by taking overall responsibility and accountability for preventing work-related injury and ill health, ensuring the OH&S policy and objectives fit the organization's strategy, integrating OH&S requirements into business processes, providing resources, protecting workers from reprisals when they report incidents, and supporting a culture that backs the system's intended results.

Top management establishes an OH&S policy that commits to providing safe and healthy working conditions, to satisfying legal and other requirements, to eliminating hazards and reducing OH&S risks, to continual improvement, and to consultation and participation of workers; it must be documented, communicated, and available to interested parties.

Responsibilities and authorities for relevant roles within the OH&S system must be assigned by top management and communicated at all levels, kept as documented information; accountability for the system's performance stays with top management even where duties are delegated, including reporting on OH&S performance to top management.

The organization must establish, implement and maintain processes for consultation and participation of workers at all levels and functions — and of workers' representatives where they exist — in the development, planning, implementation, performance evaluation and improvement actions of the OH&S system, removing barriers such as language, literacy or fear of reprisal, and giving special emphasis to the involvement of non-managerial workers.

When planning the OH&S system the organization considers its context, interested-party requirements and system scope, then determines the risks and opportunities that need to be addressed to give assurance the system can achieve its intended outcomes, prevent undesired effects, and achieve continual improvement.

Hazard identification must be an ongoing and proactive process. It has to consider how work is organized and social factors (workload, hours, victimization, harassment, bullying), leadership and organizational culture; routine and non-routine activities and situations; past relevant incidents inside or outside the organization, including emergencies and their causes; potential emergency situations; the people involved — workers, contractors, visitors and others near the workplace, including workers at locations not under the organization's direct control; the design of work areas, processes, installations, machinery and equipment; situations occurring in the vicinity of the workplace that can injure workers; and actual or proposed changes and changes in knowledge about hazards.

The organization must establish processes to assess OH&S risks from the identified hazards, taking into account the effectiveness of existing controls, and to determine and assess the other risks related to the establishment, implementation, operation and maintenance of the OH&S management system; the assessment methodologies and criteria must be defined with respect to scope, nature and timing so they are proactive rather than reactive, and maintained as documented information.

The organization must establish processes to assess OH&S opportunities to enhance OH&S performance — accounting for planned changes to the organization, its policies, processes or activities, possibilities to adapt work, work organization and the working environment to workers, and possibilities to eliminate hazards and reduce OH&S risks — as well as other opportunities for improving the OH&S management system.

The organization must have processes to determine and access the up-to-date legal requirements and other requirements applicable to its hazards, OH&S risks and management system, work out how they apply and what needs communicating, and account for them when building and running the system, retaining documented information on them.

The organization plans the actions it will take to address its risks and opportunities, its legal and other requirements, and its emergency preparedness, integrates those actions into OH&S system processes or other business processes, and evaluates their effectiveness, considering the hierarchy of controls and outputs of the system when planning.

Measurable OH&S objectives must be set at relevant functions and levels to maintain and continually improve the system and OH&S performance; they take account of applicable requirements, risk and opportunity assessment results, and consultation outcomes, are monitored, communicated and updated as appropriate, and are kept as documented information.

For each OH&S objective the organization plans what will be done, which resources are required, who is responsible, when it will be completed, and how the results — including monitoring indicators — will be evaluated, integrating the actions into business processes where practicable.
The organization must determine and provide the resources needed to establish, implement, maintain and continually improve the OH&S management system.

The organization determines the necessary competence of workers who affect or can affect OH&S performance, ensures they are competent on the basis of education, training or experience — including the ability to identify hazards — takes actions to acquire and maintain competence where needed, evaluates the effectiveness of those actions, and retains documented evidence of competence.

Workers must be made aware of the OH&S policy and objectives, their own contribution to system effectiveness and the benefits of improved performance, the implications of not conforming, relevant incidents and investigation outcomes, hazards and risks that concern them, and their right to remove themselves from situations of imminent and serious danger without reprisal.

Processes for internal and external communication relevant to the OH&S system must define what will be communicated, when, with whom and how; the organization accounts for diversity aspects (such as language and culture), ensures workers' views are considered, communicates internally among levels and functions including system changes, and communicates externally as required by legal and other obligations, retaining documented information as evidence where appropriate.

The OH&S system must include the documented information the standard requires plus what the organization itself deems necessary; when creating and updating it the organization ensures proper identification, format and review/approval, and it controls documented information so it is available, suitable and protected — governing distribution, access, storage, change control, retention and disposition, including documents of external origin.

The organization plans, implements, controls and maintains the processes needed to meet OH&S system requirements and the planned actions, by establishing operating criteria and controlling processes to those criteria, adapting work to workers, and — in multi-employer workplaces — coordinating the relevant parts of the system with other organizations.

Processes to eliminate hazards and reduce OH&S risks must apply the hierarchy of controls in order: first eliminate the hazard, then substitute with less hazardous processes or materials, then apply engineering controls and work reorganization, then administrative controls including training, and only lastly rely on adequate personal protective equipment.

The organization establishes processes for implementing and controlling planned temporary and permanent changes that impact OH&S performance — new products, services or processes, changes to work conditions, equipment, legal requirements, workforce or knowledge — reviews unintended consequences of changes, and acts to mitigate any adverse effects.
The organization must establish, implement and maintain processes to control the procurement of products and services in order to ensure their conformity to its OH&S management system.

The organization must coordinate its procurement processes with its contractors to identify hazards and to assess and control the OH&S risks arising from contractor activities and operations that impact the organization, from the organization's activities and operations that impact the contractors' workers, and from contractor activities that impact other interested parties in the workplace; the organization must ensure that the requirements of its OH&S management system are met by contractors and their workers, and its procurement processes must define and apply occupational health and safety criteria for the selection of contractors.

The organization must ensure that outsourced functions and processes are controlled: outsourcing arrangements must be consistent with legal requirements and other requirements and with achieving the intended outcomes of the OH&S system, and the type and degree of control to be applied to these functions and processes must be defined within the OH&S management system.

The organization must establish, implement and maintain processes to prepare for and respond to potential emergency situations identified during planning, including planned first-aid response, training, periodic testing and exercising of response capability, performance evaluation and revision after tests or actual emergencies, communication of duties to workers and relevant interested parties, and consideration of contractors, visitors and neighbours — with documented information on the processes and response plans maintained.

The organization determines what needs to be monitored and measured — including progress on legal and other compliance, activities related to identified hazards and risks, operational controls and OH&S objectives — the methods for monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation, the criteria and indicators, and when monitoring happens and results are evaluated; measuring equipment must be calibrated or verified as applicable, and results retained as documented information.

A process must be established to evaluate compliance with legal requirements and other requirements: the organization determines the frequency and methods of evaluation, evaluates compliance, acts if needed, maintains knowledge and understanding of its compliance status, and retains documented information of the compliance evaluation results.

Internal audits at planned intervals must verify that the OH&S management system conforms to the organization's own requirements and to the standard, and is effectively implemented and maintained; the audit programme accounts for process importance and prior audit results, auditors must be selected to ensure objectivity and impartiality, results are reported to relevant managers, workers and interested parties, nonconformities are addressed, and documented evidence of the programme and results is retained.

Top management reviews the OH&S management system at planned intervals for continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness, considering status of prior actions, changes in context and requirements, policy and objective achievement, OH&S performance trends — incidents, nonconformities, audit results, monitoring, compliance evaluations, worker consultation and participation, risks and opportunities — resource adequacy, communications with interested parties, and improvement opportunities; outputs include decisions on effectiveness, improvement needs, resources and integration, communicated to workers and their representatives, with documented evidence retained.
The organization must determine opportunities for improvement from performance evaluation results and implement the actions necessary to achieve the intended outcomes of its OH&S management system.

When an incident or nonconformity occurs, the organization must react in a timely manner, take action to control and correct it and deal with consequences, evaluate — with participation of workers and involvement of other relevant interested parties — the need for corrective action to eliminate root causes so it does not recur or occur elsewhere, review existing OH&S risk assessments, determine and implement corrective actions in line with the hierarchy of controls, assess related risks before acting, review corrective-action effectiveness, make system changes if needed, and retain documented information on incidents, nonconformities, actions taken and their results, communicating this to relevant workers and interested parties.

The suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the OH&S management system must be continually improved by enhancing performance, promoting a culture that supports the system, promoting worker participation in implementing improvement actions, communicating relevant improvement results to workers and their representatives, and maintaining documented evidence of continual improvement.
